reto is herewith enclosed.

(Sgd.) W.A. McLEAN.
AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, October 29, 1923.

SIR - I beg to acknowledge the receipt of your letter of the 11th inst., (No. 23034 - 2) in reply to mine of the 9th inst.,
respecting a payment of $12,814.42 to the Ontario Department of Public Highways in connection with the Highway
through the Tyendinaga Indian Reserve.

It appears from your reply that under the Provincial Highways Act a portion of all expenditure on Provincial Highways
within any county is chargeable against the corporation of that county, and that the proportions so chargeable were
fixed at 30 per cent of the expenditure for 1919 and 20 per cent for 1920. It further appears that the county of Hastings
objected to being held responsible for expenditure within the Indian Reserve and that accordingly your department
agreed to relieve the county from liability for such expenditure.

The amount paid by you to the Province of Ontario on account of construction was $12,589.32 being 30 per cent of
$14,395.78 for 1919, and 20 per cent of $41,352.93 for 1920, and $225.10 on account of maintenance for 1920 being
20 per cent of $1,125.50.

I beg to point out that the Department of Railways and Canals had already paid to the Province of Ontario the sum of
$16,168.29, being 40 per cent of $40,420.72 the amount established by the Highways Commission as being the actual,
necessary and reasonable cost to December 31, 1920, of the Highway through the Tyendinaga Reserve.



=== EXTRACT FROM HERE (pages 598-601) ===
<!-- page 598 -->
You will note that while the cost of construction to December 31, 1920, is given by the Ontario Department of
Highways as $55,748.71 the cost as passed by the Federal Highways Commission as being necessary and reasonable
was $40,420.72, a difference of $15,327.99.

I am of opinion that any contribution to the construction of this highway that your department might feel called upon
to make should be based on the reasonable cost as established by the Highways Commission, not on the actual amount
paid out by the Ontario Government. At the same time I think that all payments of this nature should be authorized by
the Governor in Council, and have accordingly to request you to obtain the authority of Council for this payment.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

Overpayments on Account of Salary to Agent J. Weir

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, June 12, 1923.

SIR, - I beg to ask your attention to the payments made since April 1st, 1919, to John Weir, Indian Agent, on account
of salary.

Mr. Weir was originally graded as Indian Agent, grade 4, effective from April 1st, 1919, the minimum salary of that
grade being $1,440 per annum. Later on his classification was changed, on account of a change in his position, to
Indian Agent, Grade 5, with a minimum salary of $1,980 less $480 for house, light, rations, etc., received. During the
fiscal year 1910 - 20 he was paid a salary of $1,200, to which was afterwards added arrears to the amount of $300,
making the total salary for that year $1,500, the minimum of grade 5 less $480 for allowances; from April 1st, 1920, he
was paid at the rate of $1,620, the department evidently assuming that his appointment was a permanent one. On
February 2nd, 1922, a certificate was, issued by the Civil Service Commission increasing his salary to $1,740, effective
from October 1st, 1921, and on July 15th, 1922, a further certificate was issued increasing his salary to $1,860 from
October 1st, 1922. The first of these certificates was acted upon and he was paid at the rate of $1,740 from October 1st,
1921, the second certificate, however, was not acted upon, as on August 29th, 1922, the Civil Service Commission
notified you that their attention had been drawn to the fact that Mr. Weir was a temporary employee who had been
recommended for permanency under the blanketing-in regulations and that, accordingly, the two certificates previously
issued for salary increases were cancelled. Mr. Weir was subsequently made permanent under the blanketing-in
regulations, effective from April 1st, 1921. The following statements show the amounts due Mr. Weir, each year,
according to the regulations and the amounts actually paid him, -

Salary, according to Regulations

1919 - 20 Acting Agent, Grade 4, April 1 - Aug. 31 $600 00
1919 - 20 Acting Agent, Grade 5, Sept. 1 - March 31 875 00
1920 - 21 Acting Agent, Grade 5, April 1 - March 31 1,500 00
1921 - 22 Agent, Grade 5, April 1 - March 31        1,500 00
1922 - 23 Agent, Grade 5, April 1 - March 31        1,620 00
Total     ...                                       $6,095 00

<!-- page 599 -->
Salary as Paid

1919 - 20, including $300 arrears $1,500 00
1920 - 21, April 1st - March 31st   1,620 00
1921 - 22, April 1st - Sept. 30th   810 00
1921 - 22, October 1st - March 31st 870 00
1922 - 23, April 1st - March 31st   1,740 00
...                                 $6,540 00

From this it would appear that Mr. Weir has been overpaid $445 during the four years.

As the payments up to the time you were notified of the cancellation of the certificates granting the increases were
made in good faith and had at the time the authority of the Commission, I think it might be difficult to establish a legal
claim against Mr. Weir for the overpayments, but, at the same time I am of opinion that he should be called upon to
refund the overpayments made since the cancellation of those certificates which would amount to $70, being for seven
months at the difference between $1,740 and $1,620 a year.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

Painting Buildings at Blackfoot Agency - Temporary Diversion of Trust Funds

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, February 23, 1923.

SIR, - On July 27th last Trust Fund cheque No. 2951 was issued for the amount of $700 in favour of G.H. Gooderham,
agent at the Blackfoot reserve, as an advance for painting the agency buildings.

I have received an account for Mr. Gooderham's expenditure under this advance, the items being, as follows: -

July 22 - T.W. Davidson, advance on contract              $150 00
July 29 - A.O. Forland, on account of Davidson's contract 66 00
Aug. 15 - T.W. Davidson, payment on contract              200 00
Aug. 28 - T.W. Davidson, payment on contract              40.00
Aug. 29 - T.W. Davidson, balance due on contract          181 25
Aug. 29 - T.W. Davidson, extra for glazing storm windows 7 00
Total                                                     644 25
Unexpended balance                                        55 75
...                                                       $700 00

It will be noticed from the above, that $216 of the payments were made by Mr. Gooderham before the departmental
cheque could actually have reached him. Kindly let me know what funds he would have at his disposal from which

<!-- page 600 -->
he could make these payments. What authority had Mr. Gooderham for making a payment to A.O. Forland, on account
of Davidson's contract? Such authority should have been attached to the statement as a voucher.

I should also be glad to receive any evidence you may have that the various payments made on account of Davidson's
contract were only made after work, to at least that value, had been satisfactorily executed by him.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, OTTAWA, March 13, 1923.

SIR, - In reply to your letter of the 23rd ultimo, respecting the payment of $700 made to Mr. G.H. Gooderham, Indian
Agent Blackfoot Reserve, by Trust Fund Cheque No. 2951; I beg to enclose for your information copy of a letter
received from Mr. Gooderham in which he explains why be made a payment. of $66 to Mr. A.O. Forland.

In regard to evidence that the various payments made on account of this contract were made only after the work had
been satisfactorily executed, I may say that the Agent certified to the correctness of the accounts, which is satisfactory
evidence to the Department that the contract was properly carried out, as the Department has such confidence in the
Agent that he would not certify to the accounts had it been otherwise.

In regard to the funds which Mr. Gooderham drew upon to make the payments until he received the cheque from the
Department, I may say that these were Agency Trust Funds which are accounted for in his monthly cash statements.

Your obedient servant,
J.D. MCLEAN, Asst. Deputy and Secretary.

WM. KEARNS, Asst. Auditor General.

BLACKFOOT AGENCY, GLEICHEN, ALTA., March 6, 1923.

SIR, - In reply to your letter fyle 31 - 104 dated 28th February, re painting the Agency buildings, I beg to inform you
that W.T. Davidson had the contract and one of the men working for him was A.O. Forland. This man had to leave for
the coast on July 22nd, and Davidson gave him an order on the Agency for the amount of wages due to be paid from
money due on the contract. Forland was given a cheque on the Trust Fund account in the local bank for $66. The
advance for this work had not yet arrived from Ottawa and Forland could not leave without his money, therefore, I
could not see any other way out of the matter. The advance $700 was not received until Aug. 11th. Immediately the
advance was received an adjustment was made.

The work was inspected by the Indian Agent before payments were made. There was no other person to inspect and the
buildings painted were the houses of the employees and the Indian office.

I am forwarding the written authority from Mr. Davidson for the payment of the $66 as requested.

Your obedient servant,
G.H. GOODERHAM, Indian Agent.

Asst. Deputy and Secretary of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

<!-- page 601 -->
AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, June 22, 1923.

SIR, - Let me refer you to your letter of March 13th last (File No. 31 - 104), respecting an advance of $700 made to
Mr. G.H. Gooderham, Indian Agent at the Blackfoot Reserve, by Trust Fund cheque No. 2951, for painting the Agency
Buildings.

In reply to that part of my letter of February 23rd, in which I say that I shall be glad to receive any evidence you may
have that the various payments made to Davidson on account of his contract were made only after work to at least that
value had been satisfactorily executed by him, you say that "the Agent certified to the correctness of the accounts,
which is satisfactory evidence to the Department that the contract was properly carried out, as the Department has such
confidence in the Agent that he would not certify to the accounts had it been otherwise."

I beg to point out that not only has your department to be satisfied as to the correctness of an account, but this office
also must be satisfied and must be in a position to satisfy Parliament as to its correctness. For that reason a definite
certificate such as is provided for by Section 45 of the Consolidated Revenue and Audit Act, should be given in each
case. In the case under discussion Mr. Gooderham should have given a definite certificate to the effect that the work
had been performed and that the price charged was according to contract, and should also have certified that the
advances made from time to time to Mr. Davidson were only made after work to at least the amount of the advances
had been satisfactorily performed.

You further state in your letter that pending receipt of funds from Ottawa, Mr. Gooderham drew upon his Agency
Trust Funds to make payments to the contractor. This diversion of Trust Funds, even temporarily, for any purpose
other than that for which they are held is a practice that should not be allowed in any case, but such Trust Funds
should be guarded jealously for the special purpose for which they were placed in trust.

I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs, Ottawa.

Buildings, Samson's Reserve - Unsatisfactory Certificates for Progress Payments

AUDIT OFFICE, OTTAWA, March 3, 1923.

SIR, - I have to request that you kindly furnish me with an explanation of the following three payments made during
last summer to W.J. Baldry, Wetaskiwin, for material supplied and labour performed under contract in the erection of
a farming instructor's house on Samson's reserve, Hobbema agency.

On August 25th, a certificate was issued by Mr. C.W. Kirby, Indian Agent, who appears to have acted as building
inspector, to the effect that material had been supplied and labour performed to the value of $1,168.30 and
recommending an advance of $1,000 to Mr. Baldry. This advance was made by cheque No. 3035.
